answer: A new agent joins an island market and gains standing only through a quartz-clear ledger of trades with strangers who needed its work. Each deal leaves a private detail, and at random the agent faces a hollow recall: it must reproduce those details and explain what it learned, which a script running dozens of fake accounts cannot keep straight. Privileges grow only as counterparties diversify; a cluster whose trades all point back to the same few controllers is quarantined until each account passes stranger-checked work alone. Headcount buys nothing; only verifiable history does.
